evidence: The hand-drawn Neoproterozoic cladogram (Neoprot_cladogram_June29.pdf) draws rifting (crimson) on the Congo north/east-margin rows at ca. 889-789 Ma and on its southern and eastern margins at ca. 820-729 Ma; the model releases Congo from Laurentia into the spin-axis frame at 850 Ma.

Rift box (crimson) on the Sao Francisco row of the hand-drawn Neoproterozoic cladogram (Neoprot_cladogram_June29.pdf) spans ca. 905-859 Ma; the model moves Sao Francisco from Amazonia to the Congo frame at 870 Ma.

event_label: Afif arc domain activated; Halaban suturing comes later
evidence: The Afif Terrane arc-domain feature becomes valid at 840 Ma in the Merdith v1.1b geometry (ANS-GC1 domain_age_ledger: a model-feature activation, not subaerial emergence). The hand-drawn Neoproterozoic cladogram (Neoprot_cladogram_June29.pdf) shows arc crust (pink) on Afif-Abas at ca. 848-819 Ma and its Halaban suturing (54) only at ca. 680-617 Ma, which this model does not encode as a handoff.

Hijaz arc-domain geometry is valid from 850 Ma in Merdith v1.1b (ANS-GC1 domain_age_ledger; native domain age, not subaerial emergence); the hand-drawn Neoproterozoic cladogram (Neoprot_cladogram_June29.pdf) shows juvenile arc crust (purple) on the Hijaz & Gebeit-Gabgaba row at ca. 853-824 Ma.

Accretion boxes 41 (Bi'r Umq) and 42 (Nakasib) on the Jiddah and Hijaz rows of the hand-drawn Neoproterozoic cladogram (Neoprot_cladogram_June29.pdf) span ca. 781-760 Ma; the model moves Hijaz from Gebeit/Gabgaba onto Jiddah at 780 Ma.

Egyptian Desert domain is valid from 780 Ma in Merdith v1.1b (ANS-GC1 domain_age_ledger; not literal subaerial emergence) while its rotation sequence starts at 820 Ma. The hand-drawn Neoproterozoic cladogram (Neoprot_cladogram_June29.pdf) shows juvenile arc crust (purple) on the Midyan & Egyptian Desert row at ca. 780-751 Ma.
Midyan domain is valid from 780 Ma in Merdith v1.1b (ANS-GC1 domain_age_ledger; native domain age, not subaerial emergence) while its rotation sequence starts at 820 Ma.

Atmur-Delgo domain is valid from 750 Ma in Merdith v1.1b (ANS-GC1 domain_age_ledger). The hand-drawn Neoproterozoic cladogram (Neoprot_cladogram_June29.pdf) puts its accretion (46, Atmur-Delgo) at ca. 721-700 Ma, but the model keeps it fixed to Northeast Africa throughout, so that later collision has no handoff.

event_label: Midyan-Eastern Desert accretion to the older kernel
evidence: Collins et al. (2021) discuss ca. 715 Ma Midyan-Eastern Desert accretion to the older kernel (ANS-GC1 README). The hand-drawn Neoproterozoic cladogram (Neoprot_cladogram_June29.pdf) draws accretion 44-46 (Yanbu, Allaqi, Atmur-Delgo) at ca. 721-700 Ma on the Midyan & Egyptian Desert row.
reference: Collins et al. (2021), Communications Earth & Environment, https://doi.org/10.1038/s43247-021-00149-z

evidence: Ar Rayn domain is valid from 700 Ma in Merdith v1.1b (ANS-GC1 domain_age_ledger; native domain age, not subaerial emergence) while its rotation sequence starts at 710 Ma.

event_label: Allaqi-Heiani suture: ophiolite emplaced before 709 Ma
evidence: Wadi Allaqi ophiolite emplacement predates the crosscutting ASH-1 quartz diorite (709 +/- 4 Ma), local stitching of the Allaqi-Heiani suture (ANS-CON-0003). The model keeps Egyptian Desert fixed to Gebeit/Gabgaba from 820 to 410 Ma, so this suture has no handoff to attach to; Wadi Ghadir back-arc oceanic crust at 697.8 +/- 4.2 Ma (Zoheir et al. 2022) also postdates the model's fusion.
reference: Ali et al. (2010), Gondwana Research 18(4), 583-595, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.gr.2010.03.002

event_label: Oman (on India) pole at ca. 726 Ma
evidence: Swanson-Hysell et al. (2025) place Oman (Shaat/Zalawt) at 37.5 +/- 2.5 N at ca. 726 Ma (window 743-711 Ma, ANS-CON-0005). Native Merdith 2021 reconstructs the site on Oman plate 503, carried by India, at 25.98 N (residual -11.52 deg), so the frame India enters at 720 Ma does not satisfy this constraint.

In the top panel of the hand-drawn Neoproterozoic cladogram (Neoprot_cladogram_June29.pdf) the Indo-Antarctica line leaves the Laurentia line at a stop at ca. 700 Ma; the model moves Australia-Antarctica from Laurentia to the Congo frame at 700 Ma.

event_label: Kalahari northern and Gariep margin rifting
evidence: Rift boxes (crimson) on the Kalahari row of the hand-drawn Neoproterozoic cladogram (Neoprot_cladogram_June29.pdf) (Northern margin, Gariep margin) span ca. 820-720 Ma; the model moves Kalahari from Laurentia to the Congo frame at 700 Ma.

Rift boxes (crimson) on the Amazonia & Rio Apa rows of the hand-drawn Neoproterozoic cladogram (Neoprot_cladogram_June29.pdf) span ca. 661-641 and 613-593 Ma; the model moves Amazonia from Laurentia to the Congo frame at 590 Ma.

Terminal collision box (orange: 75 Rokelides, 34 Araguaia, 35 Paraguay) on the Amazonia and Brasiliano rows of the hand-drawn Neoproterozoic cladogram (Neoprot_cladogram_June29.pdf) spans ca. 551-520 Ma.

Accretion/collision boxes 27 (Borborema) and 28 (Sergipano) on the hand-drawn Neoproterozoic cladogram (Neoprot_cladogram_June29.pdf) span ca. 636-602 Ma, with the Trans-Saharan belt (orange) at ca. 615-581 Ma; the model hands Borborema to Amazonia only at 540 Ma.
Accretion box 38 (Pampean) on the Pampea, Arequipa and Antofalla rows of the hand-drawn Neoproterozoic cladogram (Neoprot_cladogram_June29.pdf) spans ca. 544-524 Ma.

Final East-West Gondwana assembly within a broad terminal Ediacaran window, 570-540 Ma, not to be conflated with earlier internal ANS sutures (ANS-CON-0006). The hand-drawn Neoproterozoic cladogram (Neoprot_cladogram_June29.pdf) draws the terminal Malagasy (74) and Arabian-Mozambique (135) collision (orange) on the Oman row at ca. 570-530 Ma.
reference: Johnson et al. (2011), Journal of African Earth Sciences 61(3), 167-232, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jafrearsci.2011.07.003; Stern et al. (2012), Precambrian Research 206-207, 159-167, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.precamres.2012.02.008

evidence: Terminal collision box 74 (Malagasy, orange) on the Antongil (India) and Azania rows of the hand-drawn Neoproterozoic cladogram (Neoprot_cladogram_June29.pdf) spans ca. 570-530 Ma.
Closure of the Beraketa suture and final assembly between the western ANS-affinity and eastern India-affinity (Anosyen) domains of Madagascar, bracketed 580-520 Ma by SHRIMP ages (ANS-CON-0023).
reference: Boger et al. (2015), Gondwana Research 28(3), 1048-1060, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.gr.2014.08.017

evidence: Same 580-520 Ma Beraketa suture window (ANS-CON-0023); Central Madagascar is not itself the Anosyen domain, so the link to this handoff is weaker than for Southern Madagascar.
reference: Boger et al. (2015), Gondwana Research 28(3), 1048-1060, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.gr.2014.08.017

event_label: Cambrian collision along the Southern Granulite Terrane
evidence: A 513 +/- 4.6 Ma metamorphic zircon population in the Manamedu plagiogranite records a Cambrian collision to post-collisional tectonothermal event (ANS-CON-0024).
